name: Three-band parallel bandpass filter-bank pad with offset, unsynced cutoff LFOs
goal: Build a pad from bandpass filters instead of low-pass: saw (+ octave-down second osc) into three parallel resonant bandpass filters set low / mid / high, each mixed to the output, each cutoff moved by a slow LFO deliberately offset in phase/value so the three bands never move in sync, then slow-attack pad envelope, ~7-voice unison, chorus and long reverb — a filter-bank pad distinct from parallel rhythmic filter chains and single-bandpass WT pads.

source.title: Sound Design 53: Pads 3 Bandpass
source.transcript_note: YouTube English auto transcript of an AI-dubbed track (original audio es-US); route auto-target-from-dub-track.

prerequisites: Synth with 3 filters routable in parallel (or 3 BiquadFilterNodes), 2 oscillators, unison, LFOs, chorus + reverb
constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Transcript is YouTube's English auto transcript of an AI-dubbed track (original Spanish); steps are procedural and cross-checked for consistency.
Be careful with resonance on bass notes; fix with EQ.
Web Audio: three BiquadFilter(type='bandpass') in parallel summed, each frequency driven by its own OscillatorNode LFO with different start phase/rate (implementation note).

steps.action: Route oscillator 1 into filter 1, filter 2 and filter 3 in parallel, each also sent to the output. Change oscillator 1 from sine to saw.
Set all three filters to bandpass with a little resonance: filter 1 low frequencies, filter 2 mids, filter 3 highs.
steps.expect: Strange combined tone with three peaks

steps.action: Give it a pad envelope: slow attack, sustain, long release.
On filter 1 cutoff add a slow LFO (global). Copy it to filters 2 and 3 but change the value/start slightly so they don't start the same or synchronize.
Enable oscillator 2 an octave lower, also into all three filters, with the same pad envelope; nudge its speed slightly so the oscillators don't move too evenly.
steps.expect: Fuller low end without phasey sync

steps.action: Add unison ~7 voices, raise volume/bass as needed; resonance amount and output mix are to taste.
Add chorus for thickness and a long-decay reverb; play chords or a single sustained note.

verification: Muting any one filter changes the pad's spectrum noticeably.
The three bands move out of sync over a long held chord.
Bass notes don't spike excessively (EQ if needed).
